solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upset with ban that's put on bike

parts.note: to be upset is to be cross, annoyed
a bar is a prohibition, a ban

explanation.surface: A cyclist is annoyed about a ban affecting their bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's put on bike' reads as a comment on the ban, but it defines the horizontal tube of a bicycle frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The top tube joining saddle post and handlebar stem on a bicycle frame is fitted as part of the bike.

clue.text: Soldiers are unable to withdraw

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers
are unable means can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Troops find they cannot pull back from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement or belief is to withdraw it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We set about the final course

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the words that precede it are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the last dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert, the pudding, is the course served last in a British meal.

clue.text: How seasick people feel on disembarking?

definitions.text: How seasick people feel on disembarking?

parts.words: How seasick people feel on disembarking?
parts.note: people who were ill at sea feel improved once they step off the boat, and they are also literally away from the ship

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in an improved state, and here also punningly means having got off the vessel.

clue.text: Conducted bag search

parts.note: to conduct a business is to run it, past tense ran
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: Officials carried out a search of a piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly and roughly, a synonym.

clue.text: Stone upturned by vermin

parts.note: read as up turned round, the little word up written backwards
mice are household vermin

explanation.surface: Rodents disturb a stone and scatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' is read cryptically as the word UP turned around, giving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: This light volcanic rock used for smoothing skin is a kind of stone.

clue.text: Steps — quiet ones

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet
an ace is a one on a playing card or die

explanation.definitionFit: A pace is a single step, so plural steps are paces.

clue.text: Cat and mouse finally finish grooming whiskers

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters that precede it are put into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word finish

explanation.surface: A cat and a mouse end up preening their whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes H from finish; 'grooming' rearranges CATMOUSEH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair on the upper lip is a man's whiskers, in a loose sense.

clue.text: Reckon to make a hundred — getting on edge, right?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a side is an edge

explanation.surface: A batsman approaching a century grows tense and checks he is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'makes a hundred' by scoring a century, which explains the nervy surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something to be so is to reckon or judge it so.

clue.text: Stress it's money on account

indicators.note: on means the money piece is placed after the account piece

parts.note: AC or a/c is the abbreviation for account
a cent is a coin, a small sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone emphasises that the cash goes on the account.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress on a syllable or word is its accent, a synonym.

clue.text: The night air?

parts.note: air is read as a tune rather than the atmosphere, a dreamy piece of music evoking the night

explanation.definitionFit: A Chopin-style piano piece suggesting night time is a tune, an air, of the night.

clue.text: It can make a man hate what is repellent

indicators.note: the phrase says the letters of the words that follow can be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A remark that hatred can be stirred in a person by something disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can make' rearranges AMANHATE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is an anathema is detested, loathed and repellent to someone.

clue.text: Takes part in demonstration but doesn't stand out

definitions.meaning: protesters occupy a building in a seated protest
literally remains seated indoors rather than standing outside

explanation.definitionFit: A seated occupation protest is the phrase's sense, and taken literally it means staying seated inside.

clue.text: He keeps an eye on the hands to avoid overtime

definitions.text: He keeps an eye on the hands to avoid overtime

parts.words: He keeps an eye on the hands to avoid overtime
parts.note: hands are read as those on a timepiece, not workers a foreman watches

explanation.definitionFit: An employee who constantly checks the time, eager to leave promptly, fits this idiom for a shirker.

clue.text: Big plunge on Swiss bank?

parts.note: bank is read as a snowy slope in Switzerland, not a financial institution, and the plunge is a headlong sled descent

explanation.walkthrough: The CRESTA RUN is a famous ice toboggan course at St Moritz in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ice toboggan course at St Moritz is a steep plunge down a Swiss slope.

clue.text: Terrible actor in trouble with debts

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters of actor are disordered

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A struggling performer is up to their neck in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means extremely bad, a synonym of terrible.

clue.text: Words are not about to stick

definitions.note: to have words is to quarrel, so plural words here means a single quarrel

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: are not contracts to aren't, written without the apostrophe
to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Someone declares that certain words won't stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Having words with someone means having a quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Acquit, but without costs

definitions.meaning: to acquit is to release someone, declaring them not guilty

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both released from an accusation and given away at no cost.

clue.text: Rough cowl on chimney in Scotland

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is the Scots word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A hood is fitted over a Scottish chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is a noun here, a ruffian, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent thug or ruffian, the same as a gangster.

clue.text: Recover one's possession?

parts.note: read as getting back a ball one has lost, or simply taking back something once held

explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost is to recover or retrieve it.

clue.text: Parking, say, behind club

indicators.note: behind places the say piece after the parking piece

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A golfer parks behind the clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A short golf club used on the green is one of a golfer's clubs.

clue.text: Come to a similar conclusion

parts.note: conclusion is read as the ending sounds of lines of verse rather than a judgement

explanation.definitionFit: Words that share ending sounds match, as lines of verse do at their ends.

clue.text: Cursory examination not repeated

definitions.meaning: something done a single time and then finished

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a quick inspection, and read as two words means done a single time and finished.

clue.text: Where to find a washer always available

definitions.meaning: a washer is the rubber ring inside a plumbing fitting
ready to be drawn upon whenever wanted

explanation.definitionFit: A washer sits within a faucet, and the idiom means ready for use at any time.

clue.text: Double-crossing woman taking on two men

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the woman's name Elizabeth
Ray is a man's name
Al is another man's name

explanation.surface: A woman cheats on her partner by taking up with two men.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-crossing someone is betraying them, the act of treachery.

clue.text: He's not at home with legal rules

definitions.text: He's not at home with legal rules

parts.note: someone not at home is out
the law is the body of legal rules

explanation.surface: A fugitive who is unwelcome under the legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive outside the protection of the law is someone at odds with legal rules.

clue.text: It can make one act straight away

indicators.note: the phrase says the letters of the words that follow can be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A remark that a short play can be produced immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can make' rearranges ONEACT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately, without delay, means the same as straight away.

clue.text: Dissipated female locked up

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman, a female
pent means shut in, confined

explanation.definitionFit: Money or a youth dissipated is wasted, squandered away.
